name: Seed and Soil Primer (Chủng Thổ Quyết)
concept: The outer gate's method, practised with the hands in the spirit fields. A Wood root breathes as the seed and an Earth root as the soil; either alone will carry a disciple through its six layers, and a root that holds both moves faster. Each layer is tied to a season of field work, so an outer disciple cannot rush it. Its sixth layer is the First Leaf: the life tree the disciple planted on the day they joined puts out its first spirit leaf. Then, if their Wood holds, the inner gate opens.
lore: Quyền Thanh Lam rewrote it in 1006, the year the sect came down to Cổ Dịch Trấn (N-thuy_vi-03). The old primer had been written for rock gardens on the ridge and would not take in the deep loam of the post town's lost gardens.

name: Emerald Haze True Canon (Thúy Vi Chân Kinh)
concept: The founder's method and the sect's name. Thúy vi is the green breath of a mountain's middle slope, the haze that rises from living leaves over wet soil. Vương Duy wrote that on a mountain road with no rain, the empty green wet the travellers' clothes. The practitioner draws qi from growing things and breathes it back out as that haze. While it is up, you mend and the foe slowly cannot evade. Like every method, it cultivates faster on land that matches it, here where Wood is strong in the place's qi, and slowly where it is not. On the Metal ridge it was slow for five centuries, and that is why the sect left the ridge.
lore: Phùng Yên Hà wrote it in her first ten years on the empty mountain (500-510), from Không Sơn Viện's quiet and her own love of landscape (yên hà). The first copy was written on mulberry paper that the haze kept damp for five centuries. It is kept at the new seat, and it is still damp.

name: Haze Walk (Vụ Bộ)
concept: A walking art. The body thins into the green haze of a forest slope, so the walker is hard to see, hard to strike and hard to follow. It is taught to the inner gate for travel and for leaving a fight. By sect rule it is never used to come at a foe unseen. In a fight it gives evasion and a short concealment, and it can lay haze on a path behind the walker to blind pursuers.
lore: This is the art in annal V015. Tất Hành Vụ taught it in 1048 to his sworn brother, a road guard. The man took it to the cape and founded Vụ Ẩn Môn on it (N-thuy_vi-07). The sect still argues over whether that was a gift or a theft.

name: Rock-Splitting Root (Liệt Thạch Căn Quyết)
concept: The cliff pine's art. It teaches Wood to grow through stone the way a pine root splits a cliff, slowly and without stopping. It hardens the body against Metal, and its arts send roots into a foe's guard to crack it. It is slower than the haze and harsher. It is taught only on the old seat, by Cù Thúy Bách and those she allows.
lore: Cù Thúy Bách wrote it on the ridge in 1010, four years after the sect went down without her. Its first line: 'The tree that grows on the cliff does not envy the tree in the garden.'

name: Green Furnace Canon (Thanh Lô Kinh)

effects.name: The Empty Mountain's Answer (Không Sơn Đáp)
effects.rule: The Furnace Spills Over / The Empty Mountain's Answer (d5 passive art): healing lost to full health is stored and fades by a tenth each second, falling as Wood damage every 3 s when the foe cannot evade or holds 5+ Wood stacks (pending technique-effects).

concept: Alchemy without a volcano. Wood begets Fire: the alchemist lights spirit wood in a clay furnace (Earth holds the heat) and feeds the flame with their own Wood qi until it burns green. Green fire is gentle on herbs and slow to spoil a batch, which is why Thúy Vi's pills are trusted from the cape to the Pivot. In a fight it is a method of slow fire and fast pills: green flame that eats the wounded faster than the whole, and a holder whose own pills and heals act sooner.
lore: Âu Dương Thanh Lô wrote it in the 520s, when the sect was too poor to buy volcano fire from the isles. He died in 932 at Bách Thảo Viện trying to tame a fire cauldron that green flame could not hold (V029). The Furnace Hall keeps the method's last page burned at the edge, as he left it.

name: Empty Mountain Sutra (Không Sơn Kinh)

effects.name: The Empty Mountain's Answer (Không Sơn Đáp)
effects.rule: The Empty Mountain's Answer (d5 passive art): healing lost to full health is stored and fades by a tenth each second, falling as Wood damage every 3 s when the foe cannot evade or holds 5+ Wood stacks (pending technique-effects).

concept: Không Sơn Viện's highest teaching, given with the hills in 500 (C100). It is built on Vương Duy's quatrain: on the empty mountain no one is seen, only voices heard; the returning light enters the deep wood and shines again on the green moss. The holder grows still until they cannot be found. Harm that reaches them is held a moment, then returns to them as healing, the way light returns to the moss at evening. It has no killing art, which Ngu Lam Sơn says is why Thôi Bất Kiến could give it away.
lore: Thôi Bất Kiến gave it to Phùng Yên Hà with the hills, his whisk and his only student (C100). Only the founder and Ngu Lam Sơn have read past its ninth layer. The traveller who heard someone reading aloud in the empty academy in 1195 (A048) heard its first lines.

name: Thanh Nang Balm Canon (Thanh Nang Dưỡng Sinh Kinh)
concept: Thanh Nang Đường's Wood-and-Water healing lineage carried out of the fallen hall to Thúy Vi's Healing House in 1101 (V018) and practised by Ngải Thanh Hao under a renewed Hall of Rules exception.
lore: Stand-in replacement for huyen_moc: Thanh Nang Đường's quiet healing lineage carried to Thúy Vi by Dư Tục Đoạn and kept by Ngải Thanh Hao.

name: Bich Ngoc Chisel Canon (Bích Ngọc Trác Thạch Công)
concept: A jade-cutter and furnace-mender's blunt Metal-and-Earth craft: heavy wedge strikes, stone-splitting palms, and an iron body hardened at the refinery.
lore: Stand-in replacement for dia_kim: the jade-cutter and furnace-mender craft kept by Lã Trác Thạch at Bích Ngọc Khoáng.

name: Cliff Hearth Breath (Nhai Táo Tức Công)
concept: The Cliff Hall servants' plain Metal breathing for thin roots who cannot enter the Wood gate: steady breath for hauling water, sweeping the founder's pine, and swinging a kitchen cleaver.
lore: Stand-in replacement for hoang_kim: the Cliff Hall servants' steady work-breath for cleavers, buckets, and stone steps.
